subject: Meteorology
title: Hurricane Hunter Flights
description: A 60-second lesson on Hurricane Hunter Flights.

hook.text: Hurricane hunters fly directly into the storm's core—dropping instruments through the eyewall into the chaos below.

buildup.text: The 53rd Weather Reconnaissance Squadron uses WC-130J aircraft to penetrate hurricanes at about 3 km altitude.

discovery.text: Dropsondes—small instrument packages—fall through the storm, radioing back pressure, temperature, and wind data.

twist.text: Center pressure readings from these flights beat satellite estimates—essential for intensity calls.

climax.text: Without hurricane hunter data, intensity forecasts would be far less accurate—satellites alone miss critical details.

punchline.text: They fly into hurricanes on purpose—so forecasts can save lives.

quiz.question: What do dropsondes measure inside a hurricane?
options: Pressure, temperature, and wind as they fall
